name: Ventive Hospitality Ltd
title: Ventive Hospitality Ltd - 544321 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Hospitality REIT-style operator: Maldives back to growth (revenue +20%, EBITDA +25%) after Q1 diesel hit, India EBITDA +8% reported (+11% adjusted); capex funded from cash, supply pipeline of ~360 keys in FY28.

we estimate H2 occupancies of north of 70%

So in FY28 we'll have both these hotels up and running

evasions.quote: Achal, if you see the numbers related to last year , it's actually flat.
As such, we don't have any hedging strategy.

summary.headline: Ventive Q2 FY27 operating EBITDA rose 11% to INR211 crores on 5% consolidated revenue growth to INR582 crores; reported PAT fell 47% on higher D&A.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was seasonally the softest quarter, yet operating revenue grew 13% and operating EBITDA 11%, with Maldives returning to growth after a fuel-hit Q1. Reported consolidated EBITDA fell 5% to INR242 crores because other income dropped on lower forex gains, ICD interest and export incentives. Reported PAT declined 47% year-on-year as depreciation and amortisation rose from INR79 crores to INR102 crores. Management guided to a stronger H2, citing Q3 business on books of about 67% and mid-teens revenue and EBITDA growth.

segments.name: India hospitality
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 11% to INR207 crores and operating EBITDA grew 8% to INR80 crores at a 39% margin. ADR rose 11% to INR12,629, occupancy up 2 points to 68%, RevPAR up 15% to INR8,606, TRevPAR up 14%. Adjusted for one-offs, India EBITDA would have grown 11% vs 5% reported.

segments.name: Maldives hospitality
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 20% to INR213 crores and operating EBITDA grew 25% to INR30 crores; EBITDA margin about 14% vs 15% in Q1. TRevPAR rose 20% to INR45,000 and occupancy rose 3 points to 57%. Q1 EBITDA had declined 32%.

segments.name: Annuity
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 5% to INR131 crores and EBITDA was INR117 crores at a 90% margin. Committed occupancy was 98% across 3.4 million sq ft.

guidance_outlook: H2 seasonally strongest in both India and Maldives; management expects H2 occupancy above 70% and India ADR above INR14,500.
Q3 FY27: about 67% of forecast revenue on books; management guided to mid-teens revenue and EBITDA growth with occupancy above 70%.
Maldives diesel cost drag was about INR12 crores in Q2 vs about INR20 crores in Q1; management expects EBITDA and margins to strengthen further.
AC by Marriott Whitefield (Aloft Whitefield conversion) to open in Q1 FY28 and Varanasi Marriott in Q3 FY28, adding about 360 keys; Sahyadri Hills Ritz-Carlton Reserve launch remains FY29.
Solar installation at Raaya expected in January 2027, enabling about 17 hours a day generator-free operation.
capex_capacity: AC by Marriott Whitefield (Aloft Whitefield, shut for AC conversion) targeted for Q1 FY28; Varanasi Marriott targeted for Q3 FY28; management says timelines and budgets are on track.
Financial closure obtained on both Whitefield and Varanasi; company is using more of its cash surpluses to fund these projects.
Sahyadri Hills (India's first Ritz-Carlton Reserve, branded residences) master plan being finalised; FY29 launch timeline firm. Acquisition of Sahyadri Hills has increased leverage.
Solar programme across Raaya, Conrad and Anantara in progress as planned; Roha project acquisition finance drawn.
demand_pricing: India: growth on both rate and occupancy; MICE contributed 7% of revenue at JW Marriott Pune and Ritz-Carlton Pune; JW Marriott Pune hosted BRICS Communications Ministers Meeting with around 5,000 delegates over 11 days.

Maldives: occupancy gain of 3 points to 57% during an off-season affected by elevated airfares and lower tourist arrivals; diesel averaged about $1.1/litre in Q2, about 1.5x last year, down about 31% from the April-May peak.
Ritz-Carlton Pune launched YA:LA Mediterranean restaurant, expected to generate INR1.5-2 crores a month; Ritz-Carlton Pune received its first MICHELIN Key.

Other income fell about 50%: forex gains were INR21 crores vs INR48 crores last year; ICD interest ended after repayment; INR4 crores export incentive no longer available. No hedging strategy in place.
Aloft Whitefield and some Hilton Goa wings closed for refurbishment in the quarter, and the new wage code added employee cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Maldives EBITDA margin fall from Q1 (15%) to Q2 (14%) despite diesel prices falling about 31%?
qa_highlights.answer: Ranjit Batra said the added diesel cost was INR12 crores in Q2 vs about INR20 crores in Q1, and that Q2 EBITDA was flat YoY, typical for Maldives low season. He cited pricing actions, HVAC and desalination energy savings, and solar.

qa_highlights.question: Why did effective interest cost rise QoQ, and was expensive debt taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Paresh Bafna said acquisition finance for the Roha project and a 25 bps policy rate increase (about 8-10 bps passed through to the Ventive portfolio) raised costs. He said rates remain competitive.

qa_highlights.question: What is the colour on Q3 for India and Maldives, including MICE?
qa_highlights.answer: Batra said H1 operating revenue grew 10% and operating EBITDA 2%; for Q3, about 67% of forecast revenue is on the books, with mid-teens revenue and EBITDA growth and occupancy above 70%.

qa_highlights.question: Is there hedging against forex-driven swings in other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Bafna said there is no hedging strategy; the drop reflects lower forex gains (INR21 crores vs INR48 crores), ended ICD interest income and the absence of a INR4 crores export incentive.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Whitefield and Varanasi Marriott projects on time and budget?
qa_highlights.answer: Shoaib Shariff said timelines and budgets are on track: Aloft Whitefield (AC by Marriott) in Q1 FY28 and Varanasi in Q3 FY28, adding about 360 keys; financial closure is done and cash surpluses fund capex.

risks_watch: Maldives diesel: still about 1.5x last year's level, and the Q1 fuel shock showed sensitivity; solar roll-out (Raaya January 2027) is the mitigant.
Reported PAT down 47% on D&A rising to INR102 crores; monitor depreciation trajectory as Whitefield and Varanasi open.
Other income is volatile (forex, ICD repayment, export incentives) and unhedged; reported EBITDA diverges from operating EBITDA.
Leverage up to 1.6x net debt/EBITDA after Sahyadri Hills; interest costs rising with acquisition finance and rate changes.
Execution risk on Whitefield (Q1 FY28) and Varanasi (Q3 FY28) openings and the FY29 Sahyadri Hills launch.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on Maldives recovery and H2 bookings, with a few admissions: India EBITDA growth was held back by refurbishments and the wage code, and PAT decline was framed upfront. Answers on the Maldives margin and interest cost were somewhat defensive, leaning on seasonality and 'competitive' rates.
key_quotes: Double-digit growth in the monsoon quarter in TRevPAR and RevPAR of both 18% each is something I'm really proud of.
I'll be upfront, EBITDA could have grown faster. This quarter was for investing in our product.
Revenue up, EBITDA up, cash profit up.
So this quarter was not a quarter where the market did the work for us. Our teams did.
